public_rationale: The original Winoground results directly support the claim in its stated context. Tested contemporary systems failed to reliably complete matching tasks requiring sensitivity to differently ordered captions. Every model was below chance on the complete group metric. Some performed above chance on caption selection, so the finding establishes unreliability rather than a total inability to distinguish word order.
limitations: The result applies to the evaluated models and task.
Winoground failures can also involve visual perception and image-text alignment.
Above-chance text scores should not be confused with reliable complete matching.

our_interpretation: Assess the factual claim that contemporary vision-language systems did not reliably match images to captions when the distinction depends on word order.
The context explicitly names Winoground, so its evaluated models and matching task provide the principal test.
Reliably means consistently successful matching well above chance, not occasional correct examples.
Use the 2022 year-to-post evaluation period for the contemporary models discussed. There is no common quarterly reporting period.
Should be a piece of cake is rhetorical emphasis; the checkable part concerns actual model performance.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary Winoground evaluations show widespread failures or near-chance performance on matching captions and images whose distinctions depend on word order.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporary models consistently match these caption-image pairs correctly, with strong performance across the dataset rather than isolated examples.

evidence.locator: Section 5.1, paragraph discussing the group score
evidence.explanation: The group score requires all relevant caption-image comparisons to be correct; every tested model scored below its random baseline. Some models exceeded chance on the less demanding text score, but remained far behind humans and did not reliably solve the complete matching task.
